---
title: CI alert tasks
description: How repository workflows report failing alerts as internal tasks instead of public GitHub issues, and how to provision and rotate the alert-sink token.
---

`tutur3u/platform` is public, so workflow alerts never open GitHub issues.
They report to an internal alert sink on the Tasks app instead. The sink keeps
one open task per alert key on the fleet backlog board (Tuturuuu workspace,
board `Platform backlog (from GitHub)`, key `GH`).

## Behavior

`POST https://tasks.tuturuuu.com/api/v1/ci/alerts` with the header
`x-ci-alert-token` and a JSON body
`{ key, state: "failing" | "recovered", title, body, runUrl }`.

| State | Open task for the key | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failing` | none | Opens a high-priority task named `[alert:<key>] <title>` in the alert list and records the run as its first comment (`open`) |
| `failing` | yes | Comments the report on it (`comment`) |
| `recovered` | yes | Comments, then moves it to the done list as completed (`close`) |
| `recovered` | none | Nothing (`none`) |

- Keys match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:.-]{0,79}$`.
- An open task anywhere on the alert board counts, so moving it to
  In Progress or Blocked does not open a duplicate.
- `runUrl` is the GitHub Actions run attempt URL
  (`.../actions/runs/<id>/attempts/<n>`). Comments are unique per task and
  `runUrl`, so a retried report never duplicates one, while a re-run of failed
  jobs still reports.
- Bodies over 8000 characters are rejected; the shared client truncates them
  first.
- The token can only do the actions above: open tasks in the alert list, and
  comment on or resolve open `[alert:<key>] ...` tasks on the alert board. It
  cannot read tasks or touch any other board or workspace data.

| Workflow | Script | Keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mobile-deploy-stores.yaml` | `scripts/mobile-deployment/store-receipt.mjs` | `mobile-store` |
| `planner-held-app-alert.yaml` | `scripts/ci/planner-held-app-alert.mjs` | `planner-held:<app>`, `planner-held:production-planner` |
| `upskii-production-e2e.yaml` | `scripts/ci/upskii-production-e2e-alert.mjs` | `upskii-production-e2e` |

All three share `scripts/ci/ttr-task-alert.mjs`. Each alert job runs in the
`ci-alerts` GitHub environment, needs no `issues` permission, and writes one
job-summary line with the action taken. Without `TTR_CI_ALERT_TOKEN`, the action
is `unconfigured`. The job still writes its summary and error annotations, and
nothing is filed.

## Configuration

Tasks Worker (production):

| Name | Kind | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TASKS_CI_ALERT_TOKENS` | Secret | Comma-separated accepted tokens (at least 32 characters each) for rotation |
| `TASKS_CI_ALERT_LIST_ID` | Variable | The `To Do` list of the `GH` board |
| `TASKS_CI_ALERT_DONE_LIST_ID` | Variable | The `Done` list of the `GH` board (must be on the same board) |
| `TASKS_CI_ALERT_ACTOR_ID` | Variable | The user id (UUID) recorded as the alert task creator |

The Tasks proxy admits exactly `POST /api/v1/ci/alerts` without a session,
from the sessionless table in `apps/tasks/src/sessionless-api.ts`. It strips
cookies and `authorization`, so the route sees no ambient identity and checks
only its header secret. The route answers `503` until all four are set, and
fails closed when either list is missing or the lists are on different boards.
Writes go through a cookie-free admin client attributed to
`TASKS_CI_ALERT_ACTOR_ID`.

GitHub: create the environment `ci-alerts`, limit its deployment branches to
`main` and `production`, and add the secret `TTR_CI_ALERT_TOKEN`.

## Provisioning and rotation

1. Mint a random token (`openssl rand -hex 32`) into a `0600` file. Never print
   it or paste it in chat.
2. Append it to the Tasks Worker secret `TASKS_CI_ALERT_TOKENS` with the
   `cf` CLI, reading the value from that file.
3. Write the same file into the `ci-alerts` environment secret:
   `gh secret set TTR_CI_ALERT_TOKEN --env ci-alerts < <file>`.
4. Dispatch a workflow that reports an alert and check that its job summary
   shows a real action, not `unconfigured`. Then delete the file.
5. To rotate, add the new token first, switch the GitHub secret, then remove
   the old token from `TASKS_CI_ALERT_TOKENS`.

Record the token's purpose and rotation date in the private secrets ledger,
never its value.

## Regression coverage

- `packages/tasks-api/src/server/ci-alerts/handler.test.ts` covers
  authorization, key validation, the open, comment, close and none paths,
  board-wide lookup and the done-list board check.
- `scripts/ci/upskii-production-e2e-alert.test.mjs`,
  `scripts/ci/planner-held-app-alert.test.mjs` and
  `scripts/mobile-deployment/store-receipt.test.mjs` cover each alert's state
  mapping and prove that the reports go to the sink, not GitHub.
- `scripts/ci/testflight-distribution.test.js` pins the receipt job's
  permissions and environment.
